Further references will be given throughout the course. All course material,
updates, and relevant information are available on **ILIAS**.

## Introductory textbooks

- Chan, Joshua, et al. *Bayesian Econometric Methods*. Cambridge University Press, 2019.
- Gelman, Andrew, et al. *Bayesian Data Analysis*. Chapman and Hall/CRC, 2013.
- Geweke, John. *Contemporary Bayesian Econometrics and Statistics*. John Wiley & Sons, 2005.
- Koop, Gary M. *Bayesian Econometrics*. Wiley, 2003.
- Lambert, Ben. *A Student's Guide to Bayesian Statistics*. Sage Publishing, 2018.

## Core papers

- Avramov, Doron, and Guofu Zhou. "Bayesian portfolio analysis." *Annual Review of Financial Economics* 2.1 (2010): 25–47.
- Giannone, Domenico, Michele Lenza, and Giorgio E. Primiceri. "Economic predictions with big data: The illusion of sparsity." *Econometrica* 89.5 (2021): 2409–2437.
- Hill, Jennifer L. "Bayesian nonparametric modeling for causal inference." *Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics* 20.1 (2011): 217–240.
- Primiceri, Giorgio E. "Time varying structural vector autoregressions and monetary policy." *The Review of Economic Studies* 72.3 (2005): 821–852.

## Further textbooks and monographs

- Box, George E. P., and George C. Tiao. *Bayesian Inference in Statistical Analysis*. Addison-Wesley, 1973.
- Durbin, James, and Siem Jan Koopman. *Time Series Analysis by State Space Methods*. 2nd ed. Oxford University Press, 2012.
- Imbens, Guido W., and Donald B. Rubin. *Causal Inference for Statistics, Social, and Biomedical Sciences*. Cambridge University Press, 2015.
- Rasmussen, Carl E., and Christopher K. I. Williams. *Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning*. MIT Press, 2006.
- Robert, Christian P., and George Casella. *Monte Carlo Statistical Methods*. 2nd ed. Springer, 2004.
- Zellner, Arnold. *An Introduction to Bayesian Inference in Econometrics*. Wiley, 1971.

## Papers by block

### Foundations

- Geweke, John. "Bayesian inference in econometric models using Monte Carlo integration." *Econometrica* 57.6 (1989): 1317–1339.

### Computation

- Casella, George, and Edward I. George. "Explaining the Gibbs sampler." *The American Statistician* 46.3 (1992): 167–174.
- Chib, Siddhartha, and Edward Greenberg. "Understanding the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm." *The American Statistician* 49.4 (1995): 327–335.
- Gelfand, Alan E., and Adrian F. M. Smith. "Sampling-based approaches to calculating marginal densities." *Journal of the American Statistical Association* 85.410 (1990): 398–409.
- Hoffman, Matthew D., and Andrew Gelman. "The No-U-Turn sampler: adaptively setting path lengths in Hamiltonian Monte Carlo." *Journal of Machine Learning Research* 15 (2014): 1593–1623.

### Macro and policy

- Bańbura, Marta, Domenico Giannone, and Lucrezia Reichlin. "Large Bayesian vector auto regressions." *Journal of Applied Econometrics* 25.1 (2010): 71–92.
- Giannone, Domenico, Michele Lenza, and Giorgio E. Primiceri. "Prior selection for vector autoregressions." *The Review of Economics and Statistics* 97.2 (2015): 436–451.
- Madigan, David, and Adrian E. Raftery. "Model selection and accounting for model uncertainty in graphical models using Occam's window." *Journal of the American Statistical Association* 89.428 (1994): 1535–1546.
- Rubio-Ramírez, Juan F., Daniel F. Waggoner, and Tao Zha. "Structural vector autoregressions: theory of identification and algorithms for inference." *The Review of Economic Studies* 77.2 (2010): 665–696.

### Finance

- Chipman, Hugh A., Edward I. George, and Robert E. McCulloch. "BART: Bayesian additive regression trees." *The Annals of Applied Statistics* 4.1 (2010): 266–298.
- Jacquier, Eric, Nicholas G. Polson, and Peter E. Rossi. "Bayesian analysis of stochastic volatility models." *Journal of Business & Economic Statistics* 12.4 (1994): 371–389.
- Kim, Sangjoon, Neil Shephard, and Siddhartha Chib. "Stochastic volatility: likelihood inference and comparison with ARCH models." *The Review of Economic Studies* 65.3 (1998): 361–393.
- Kozak, Serhiy, Stefan Nagel, and Shrihari Santosh. "Shrinking the cross-section." *Journal of Financial Economics* 135.2 (2020): 271–292.

## How the reading maps to the course

The textbooks cover the foundations and computation blocks. Chan et al. and Koop
are the closest fit for the econometric framing; Gelman et al. (BDA) is the
reference for general Bayesian modelling and diagnostics; Lambert is the gentlest
entry point if the material is new to you.

The core papers anchor the applications block: Primiceri (2005) for time-varying
VARs and state-space models, Giannone et al. (2021) for shrinkage in
high-dimensional forecasting, Avramov and Zhou (2010) for Bayesian portfolio
choice, and Hill (2011) for Bayesian causal inference.

## How the supplementary material supports the lectures

The weekly sequence and assigned readings remain those in the [schedule](schedule.qmd).
The following supplementary sources develop the intuition and intermediate algebra used
in the notes. The Python exercises translate these ideas into the scheduled applications.

| Weeks | Supplementary source | Use in this course |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1–2 | Audronė Virbickaitė and Martina Zaharieva, supplied UPM Classes 1–2 and Case 2 | Conditional probability, sequential updating, conjugate kernels, prior elicitation and predictive integration |
| 3–5 | Supplied UPM Class 3 and Cases 3–5 | Integration, importance weights, Gibbs conditionals, Metropolis ratios, latent variables and logistic regression |
| 2, 6, 9, 11 | Supplied UPM Class 5 | Regression priors, regularisation, model evidence and variable selection |
| 14, optional extension | Supplied UPM Class 4 | Variational approximation and its contrast with posterior sampling |
| 2, 4, 8, 10 | Greenberg (2008), *Introduction to Bayesian Econometrics* | Regression algebra (4.1–4.3), MCMC (7), regression sampling (8.1), TVP (10.3), treatment and endogeneity (11.1–11.2) |
| 3–5, 9, 12 | Geweke (2005), *Contemporary Bayesian Econometrics and Statistics* | Posterior simulation (4), Metropolis-within-Gibbs (4.6.2), model comparison and checks (8) |
| 6–9 | Luc Bauwens, supplied *Bayesian Econometrics* lecture notes (6 April 2013); Sylvia Frühwirth-Schnatter, supplied lecture slides | Multivariate regression and VARs, prediction, and state-space reasoning |
| 13, supplementary derivation | Frey and Pohlmeier (2026), supplied *Bayesian Shrinkage Regressions for the Global Minimum Variance Portfolio*, Section 2.2 | Reference-portfolio regression identity and the interpretation of shrinkage as allocation regularisation |

UPM is the label of the supplied teaching-material collection. Later applications—BVAR
identification, causal BART, stochastic volatility and Gaussian processes—use the
specialist literature assigned to those weeks. The source PDFs are reading material;
the site provides adapted explanations and derivations rather than reproducing the books.
